subject: Payment timing & tax allocation for Redwood Order Form
messages:
From: Marcelo Ruiz <marcelo@stellara.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Noor <samira.noor@stellara.io>, Elise White <elise.white@primelegal.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Order Form (pricing schedule & tax)

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for sending over the updated Order Form. Elise and I did a first pass and flagged two items that need clarification before our procurement team can approve:

1) Tax allocation: The current draft says Redwood will "gross up" and remit any applicable VAT/GST. We need explicit confirmation that Stellara will not be liable for withholding tax on US-dollar invoices and that Redwood will provide tax receipts suitable for VAT reclaim.

2) Invoicing cadence / payment terms: Your order form lists quarterly invoicing for committed spend with Net 45 payment terms. Our standard is monthly invoices and Net 60 for initial enterprise customers with new payment profiles. Can Redwood accommodate monthly invoices for the first year, or alternatively accept Net 60?

Also attached a brief annex with our redline suggestions on the tax section.

Appreciate a quick call if needed — procurement is hoping to get this wrapped by end of week.

Thanks,
Marcelo
(Attachment: Tax_Annex_Stellara.pdf (pdf))

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marcelo Ruiz <marcelo@stellara.io>, Samira Noor <samira.noor@stellara.io>
Cc: Elise White <elise.white@primelegal.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Order Form (pricing schedule & tax)

Marcelo — thanks for the callout and the annex. Short answers up front: we can be flexible on invoice cadence for year one; tax treatment needs a bit more nuance.

Proposal:
- Invoicing: Redwood will switch to monthly invoices for the first 12 months of the term, then revert to quarterly unless you opt in to continue monthly.
- Net terms: We can agree to Net 60 for the initial 12-month commitment as a concession for new enterprise onboarding.
- Tax: Redwood cannot be the party that bears withholding tax for amounts legitimately required by customer jurisdiction (we collect and remit where Redwood is required). However we will: (a) confirm Redwood will issue VAT/GST-compliant invoices and receipts; (b) add a mutual cooperation clause for tax documentation and (c) include language committing Redwood to reasonable assistance for Stellara's VAT reclaim.

I attached our current Order Form (v2) with a few inline notes on the tax paragraph. If that framing works, I can loop in our Legal (Ben and Soojin) to finalize wording that Elise is comfortable with.

Next steps: if you’re available, I can set a 30-minute sync tomorrow to greenline final language.

Regards,
Priyom
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | priyom.das@redwood.com
(Attachment: Redwood_OrderForm_v2.docx (docx))

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-18T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Redwood Order Form (pricing schedule & tax) — Stella asks

Team — forwarding Stellara's notes (see attached annex). Key asks: monthly invoices year 1 (fine), Net 60 instead of Net 45 (we can concede), and more careful wording on tax/gross-up.

Open items where I need legal ops guidance:
- Tax gross-up language: Stellara expects Redwood to provide VAT receipts and 'assistance' for reclaim. Their counsel is pushing that Redwood "shall be responsible for any VAT/GST or other indirect taxes payable on the Services." That is too broad. Recommend we offer: Redwood will invoice VAT/GST where applicable and provide compliant receipts; customer remains responsible for any customer-side withholding unless Redwood is required by law to withhold.
- PO vs invoice cadence: they asked for monthly invoices and Net 60 for year 1. Commercial prefers Net 45 quarterly. I think concession to monthly + Net 60 is acceptable if we secure a 12-month minimum commit and include early termination fees.

Benchmarks: deal size ~ $750k ARR commit (see deal id). We should avoid setting a global precedent on gross-up. Suggest language with explicit carveouts and mutual cooperation.

Can you draft suggested language we can send to Elise? I want to keep the final exchange to one round.

Thanks — Priyom

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood Order Form (pricing schedule & tax) — suggested legal language

Priyom / team — draft language below that keeps us protected but addresses Stellara's concerns. Paste into the Order Form as a new paragraph in the Tax/Payment section:

"Taxes and Withholding: Except for taxes based on Redwood's net income, Redwood will remit and be responsible for VAT/GST or similar indirect taxes imposed on fees invoiced by Redwood, and will issue VAT/GST-compliant invoices or receipts. Customer shall be responsible for any taxes, duties, or withholdings imposed on amounts payable by Customer by applicable law. If Customer is required by law to withhold taxes, Customer shall notify Redwood in writing, provide official tax receipts, and (where allowed) gross-up amounts only to the extent required by law. The parties shall cooperate in good faith to minimize tax liabilities and provide reasonable assistance for VAT/GST reclaims"

Commercial compromise on payment: accept monthly invoices + Net 60 for the first 12 months provided we: (1) capture a 12-month minimum commitment and (2) add a fee tier if payment delays exceed 60 days (1.5% monthly interest after 60 days).

I'll also prepare a redline for the Order Form and propose the DocuSign envelope once Stellara confirms.

Ben

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marcelo Ruiz <marcelo@stellara.io>, Samira Noor <samira.noor@stellara.io>
Cc: Elise White <elise.white@primelegal.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed compromise on invoicing & tax language — Redwood 

Marcelo / Samira / Elise — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per internal review, Redwood proposes the following compromise: 

1) Invoicing/payment: Redwood will issue monthly invoices for the first 12 months of the Term and grant Net 60 payment terms for those invoices. After month 12, Redwood will revert to quarterly invoicing with Net 45 unless Customer provides written notice to continue monthly billing. 

2) Tax clause (new paragraph inserted into the Order Form):

"Taxes and Withholding: Except for taxes based on Redwood's net income, Redwood will remit and be responsible for VAT/GST or similar indirect taxes imposed on fees invoiced by Redwood, and will issue VAT/GST-compliant invoices or receipts. Customer shall be responsible for any taxes, duties, or withholdings imposed on amounts payable by Customer by applicable law. If Customer is required by law to withhold taxes, Customer shall notify Redwood in writing, provide official tax receipts, and (where allowed) gross-up amounts only to the extent required by law. The parties shall cooperate in good faith to minimize tax liabilities and provide reasonable assistance for VAT/GST reclaims"

3) Minimum commitment: Stella's signature on the Order Form will confirm a 12-month minimum committed spend of $750,000; early termination without cause will trigger a payment equal to the lesser of the remaining committed fees or a 6-month pro rata charge.

4) Late payment: invoices unpaid 60 days after invoice date will accrue interest at 1.5% per month.

If that is acceptable, we will: (a) update the Order Form with the attached redline, (b) send a DocuSign envelope for signature, and (c) issue the first monthly invoice upon signature.

DocuSign link (preview): https://app.docusign.com/REDWOOD/Envelope/0a1b2c3d4e
(Attachment: Redwood_OrderForm_v2.docx (docx))

Please confirm and we’ll send the final redline today.

Best,
Priyom
